core_decision.reason: The open cohort is generated from public plate scans and public catalogues with an explicit independence audit and release-bound integrity hashes; it need not clone the private/closed catalogue to test whether a temporal association independently replicates.

open_cohort_binding.footprint_rule: all POSS-I red plates whose centre declination >= -3.0 deg; an empty plate-centre gap between -5 and -1 deg makes the 642-plate northern footprint threshold-insensitive within that gap
open_cohort_binding.stage_S0_semantics: source on a POSS-I plate surviving the release filter/veto chain; not a confirmed transient or vanishing-object identity
selection_notes: released coordinates include a per-tile Gaia astrometric refit
USNO-B is an added third veto relative to the paper-parity Gaia+PS1 arm; paper-parity is reported as 16.2% larger on the validated subset

independence_gate.mechanism: tools/audit_independence.py scans both working tree and git history for private-reference catalogue markers
independence_gate.admission_interpretation: This is evidence of source independence of the published repository/release, not proof that every scientific selection choice is unbiased.

astrometry_artifact_model.important_version_note: Older 207/633 and ~2.344 arcsec figures refer to an earlier audit footprint/version and must not be substituted for the bound 642-plate release.
astrometry_artifact_model.janus_consequence: WCS quality and repair status become mandatory nuisance variables in any temporal association model because a time/plate-correlated astrometric failure can create false candidate-rate structure.

watters_2026.note: Critical reanalysis reports a one-date discrepancy while parsing the same cited public source families.

sipri_open_digitization_sensitivity.source_lineage: open structured digitization of SIPRI Nuclear Explosions 1945-1998
sipri_open_digitization_sensitivity.warning: NON_UW is not asserted to equal the paper's 'above-ground' definition; CRATER and safety-experiment classifications require an explicit physical-policy arm rather than silent recoding.

frozen_calendar_arms_for_execution.warning: includes event types that are not physically equivalent to atmospheric/above-ground detonations
still not a complete physical definition of atmospheric/above-ground exposure

frozen_calendar_arms_for_execution.rule: separate AIRDROP/ATMOSPH/TOWER/SURFACE/BARGE/SHIP from UW, CRATER and safety-experiment classes; publish exclusions and sensitivity variants

nuclear_calendar_audit.decision_rule: No association is called robust unless direction and material effect survive reasonable calendar-arm definitions; a result dependent on the 124-vs-125 membership discrepancy is classified CALENDAR_FRAGILE.

plate_metadata_join.source: IRSA browsable dss1red full-plate FITS files + STScI DSS metadata/header conventions
plate_metadata_join.known_remote_file_size_example: IRSA directory lists 374M for each early XE plate including XE325
plate_metadata_join.preferred_io: HTTP Range/stream only complete FITS header blocks; do not download image arrays for temporal-only tests
required_fields: DATE-OBS or equivalent plate date fields
exposure duration keyword(s) after exact header verification
plate_metadata_join.reason: STScI confirms individual-image provenance is in FITS headers, but JANUS will not assume a particular exposure keyword without reading actual plate headers.

temporal_replication_design.primary_exposure: nuclear calendar window, sensitivity across frozen calendar arms
mandatory_normalization: usable processed tiles or exposed sky area
mandatory_nuisance_covariates: WCS plate-level correction flag and magnitude
later_physical_covariates: Sun/Earth-shadow geometry for hypotheses that predict reflected sunlight
statistics: negative-binomial count model with log(opportunity) offset
temporal_replication_design.anti_p_hacking_rule: calendar definitions, opportunity denominator, covariates, and primary model are frozen before viewing nuclear-window coefficients in the open cohort.

current_external_evidence_context.bruehl_villarroel_2025: reports RR~1.45 and p=0.008 for +/-1-day nuclear window in the original processed cohort
current_external_evidence_context.watters_et_al_2026: reports the nuclear association becomes insignificant after normalization by actual POSS-I observation days and is largely determined by the Palomar schedule
current_external_evidence_context.doherty_2026: using the original supplied dataset reports replication of RR~1.45 and additional controlled/permutation support
current_external_evidence_context.hayes_2026_public_independent_pipeline: reports +1-day calendar RR=1.35, 95% CI 0.91-2.00, Fisher p=0.17; negative-binomial nightly count model with coverage exposure IRR=1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.18, p=0.71
current_external_evidence_context.janus_interpretation: The disagreement makes an independently generated, public, plate-bound cohort especially valuable as an adjudication dataset; prior results set expectations, not labels.

remaining_blockers: materialize/stream the two small public release tables in an execution environment
build and hash the 642-plate header/date table
freeze exact nuclear-calendar memberships and physical classification arms
execution_state.posterior_reason: This admission stage establishes an independent public cohort and stronger artifact model; it does not yet provide the exposure-normalized plate-day likelihoods needed for FLASH/GLINT/COPY_DEFECT/PERSISTENT model posteriors.
